title: Lightweight “PLG Signal Review Queue” mock (HubSpot view first, optional internal page later)
creator: Nikhil Sharma
description:
Context
We’re piloting PLG→sales signal routing into HubSpot. Early pilot feedback (Sales + Marketing Ops) is that raw signal volume is too high and AEs/SDRs need a fast way to triage: identify what’s real, what’s duplicate, what’s already being worked, and what should be suppressed.

This ticket produces a lightweight mock / spec for a “Signal Review Queue” experience that is:
- HubSpot-native first (saved views + properties + task queue conventions)
- Minimal engineering dependency (mostly CRM config + property hygiene)
- Designed to reduce spam and enable quick triage (what to do next is obvious)
- Extensible to an optional internal page later (if HubSpot UI limits us)

Goals
1) Define the HubSpot view layout (columns + default sorts + filters) that supports quick scanning.
2) Define the minimum set of properties required on Company + the routed “PLG Signal” activity/note to make the queue usable.
3) Provide a simple triage interaction model (acknowledge / snooze / suppress / needs SE / needs CS) that can map to HubSpot actions today.
4) Align on what is “the queue” for NA pilot (who uses it, when, and what exit criteria are).

Non-goals
- Designing a brand new full internal dashboard for Phase 1. (We can outline a Phase 3 direction.)
- Redesigning the whole HubSpot information architecture. Keep it scoped to a pilot-friendly saved view + task template conventions.

Primary users (pilot)
- AEs (NA): review new signals each morning, prioritize outreach, route to SE for technical evaluation
- SDRs (where applicable): work a subset of “intent” signals (pricing + dedicated docs + security FAQ)
- Sales Ops / HubSpot admin: monitor noise levels and ensure the queue is working
- CS (secondary): visibility to avoid conflicting outreach for existing customers

Proposed information architecture (HubSpot-first)
A) Primary queue = Saved view on Companies
Name: “PLG Signal Review Queue (NA Pilot)”
Default filter suggestions:
- PLG Signal Status = “New” OR “Re-notified”
- PLG Signal Score >= threshold (e.g., 70) OR PLG Signal Type in {Compliance, Reliability} (even if score slightly lower)
- Exclude “Suppressed until” > today
- Exclude Lifecycle Stage = “Customer” unless “Expansion = true” (avoid CS conflict)
- Exclude Existing owner type = CSM-only owned (depends on Sales Ops rules)
Default sort:
- PLG Signal Priority (High→Low)
- Then PLG Signal Created At (desc)

B) Secondary queue = HubSpot Task queue
Task template: “PLG Signal follow-up (pilot)” created by router workflow with due date = created_at + 0 business days for High priority, +1 day for Medium.
Users can work from tasks, but the saved view is the place to understand signal context.

Recommended columns (Company view)
Keep columns limited (HubSpot density). Prioritize “why is this here” and “what should I do”.
1) Company name
2) Owner
3) PLG Signal Priority (High/Med/Low)
4) PLG Signal Type (Scale / Reliability / Compliance / Expansion / Pricing)
5) PLG Signal Summary (one-line human readable string)
   - Format: “Last 7d: 3.2M tokens/day (+68% WoW), 429s on /chat.completions, Dedicated docs viewed”
6) PLG Signal Score (0–100)
7) PLG Signal Window (7d / 30d)
8) PLG Signal Created At
9) Last Contacted (date)
10) Open tasks (count) OR “Next task due”
11) Suppressed until (date) (blank if none)
12) SE Needed (Y/N) OR “Route to SE” (boolean property) — see triage model

Optional columns (toggle on for Ops, not default for AEs)
- Region (routing verification)
- Paid status (Trial / Self-serve paid / Enterprise)
- Current spend (30d)
- Re-notification count (to detect noisy accounts)

Signal note content (activity/timeline) format
We can’t rely on HubSpot users opening every attached object; the timeline note should be skimmable.
Title: “PLG Signal: Reliability risk (429 burst) — High priority”
Body template:
- What we saw (metrics, time window)
- Why it matters (customer impact risk, upgrade fit)
- Suggested next step (playbook link + discovery prompt)
- Links: company page, docs pages visited (if captured), relevant internal playbook section
Example body:
“Window: last 7d (ending 2025-05-14)
Signals:
- 429s: 18 events on /v1/chat.completions (p95 retry delay 12s)
- Token volume: 2.9M/day (+54% WoW)
- Docs intent: Dedicated capacity guide viewed 3x by 2 users
Suggested next step:
- Send ‘reliability + scaling’ email (Cadence v1 Day 0), offer Dedicated benchmark + burst capacity discussion.
- If customer mentions SLOs or isolation requirements, loop SE.
Playbook: Confluence → Sales enablement → PLG Signal Follow-up Playbook (section: Reliability)
Router details: signal_schema=v1, dedupe_key=company_id+signal_type+window_end, confidence=0.82”

Triage model (maps to HubSpot actions today)
We need a small set of consistent actions that reduce spam without creating new tooling.

Statuses (Company properties)
- PLG Signal Status: New | Working | Routed to SE | Routed to CS | Snoozed | Suppressed | Closed-Won Influence | Closed-Lost/Not a fit
- PLG Signal Disposition (required on close): Interested | Not now | Already in active motion | False positive | Support issue | Duplicate

Actions and how to do them in HubSpot (pilot)
1) Acknowledge / Working
- AE sets PLG Signal Status = Working
- Router should avoid re-notifying for X days if status is Working (suppression logic handled in ENG)

2) Snooze
- AE sets “Suppressed until” = today + 7 days (default)
- Status = Snoozed

3) Suppress (noise)
- AE sets Status = Suppressed
- Sets “Suppress reason” = False positive / Internal test / Marketing touch in progress / Support issue
- Sets “Suppressed until” = today + 30 days (default; Ops can override)

4) Needs SE
- AE sets “SE Needed” = true OR status = Routed to SE
- Router/workflow should notify SE owner (Markus Klein’s team) via task or Slack (implementation by Sales Ops/Eng; design just specifies)

5) Needs CS (existing customer expansion / conflict)
- If Company is a customer and signal indicates expansion (new workspace spikes, multi-team), set Status = Routed to CS and tag CSM

Queue operating rhythm (pilot recommendation)
- AEs check the saved view daily (10 min) + work tasks.
- Sales Ops checks volume + false-positive rate weekly; adjust thresholds/suppression.
- Any account suppressed as “False positive” should be reviewed in weekly pilot meeting to tune scoring.

Mock deliverables
1) HubSpot saved view wireframe (dense table)
- Included in Figma: “PLG Signal Review Queue v0.2” (link in comments)
- Shows recommended columns, filter chips, and a right-side ‘preview’ area concept (if HubSpot supports) but not required.

2) Property spec (minimum viable)
Company properties:
- plg_signal_priority
- plg_signal_type
- plg_signal_score
- plg_signal_summary
- plg_signal_created_at
- plg_signal_window
- plg_signal_status
- plg_signal_disposition
- plg_signal_suppressed_until
- plg_signal_re_notify_count
- plg_signal_se_needed
- plg_signal_cs_needed

3) Task template text
Task title: “PLG Signal follow-up: {{plg_signal_type}} ({{plg_signal_priority}})”
Task notes: include the one-line summary + link to playbook section.

Design decisions / trade-offs
- Kept the queue company-centric vs a separate custom object list. HubSpot custom object UI is harder to operationalize for AEs; company view is the common workflow.
- Prioritized “Signal Summary” as a single compact sentence. Without it, users must click into timeline notes too often.
- Included “Suppressed until” as a first-class column to make spam controls visible/auditable.
- Avoided new bespoke tags for every signal; we stick to a small taxonomy (Scale/Reliability/Compliance/Expansion/Pricing) for cognitive load.

Risks / open questions
- HubSpot column limits and table density: may require two saved views (AE default vs Ops debug).
- Status/disposition adoption: if AEs don’t set status, suppression rules won’t work. Consider making disposition required when closing a task.
- Preview pane feasibility: HubSpot may not show the timeline note preview without a click; if too slow, we may need a lightweight internal page Phase 3.

Phase 3 direction (optional internal page)
If HubSpot UI becomes limiting, an internal page could:
- Show a unified list of recent signals (custom object) with a true preview pane
- Provide one-click actions (snooze/suppress/reroute)
- Display signal history and dedupe decisions
Still route outcomes back to HubSpot to keep source-of-truth for GTM.

Acceptance criteria
- Mock/wireframe shared with Sales Ops (Isabelle), HubSpot admin (David), and pilot AE rep (Avery)
- Agreed list of default columns and filters for NA pilot saved view
- Agreed minimal property set and naming conventions (snake_case is fine internally; HubSpot labels should be human-friendly)
- Documented triage actions + mapping to HubSpot steps (status updates, suppression dates)

References
- HubSpot workflows/properties spec (Drive): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/hubspot-workflows-and-properties-spec.json
- PRD (Confluence): sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/plg-to-sales-signal-routing-prd.json
- Ownership/routing ADR (Confluence): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hubspot-routing-and-ownership-rules.json
comments: 2025-05-08 (Sofia Chen): Drafted v0.1 wireframe for a HubSpot Company saved view. Key insight: users need a one-line summary + explicit suppression controls; otherwise every “signal” feels like spam.

2025-05-09 (Isabelle Laurent): +1 on making ‘Suppressed until’ visible. Also recommend separating AE view vs Ops view; AEs don’t want spend columns. Please include ‘Open tasks’ so they can see if something is already being worked.

2025-05-10 (David Kim): HubSpot has practical column limits; we can do two saved views and pin the AE one. We can create properties, but would like to keep the number of booleans minimal. Can we represent SE/CS routing as a status instead of separate fields?

2025-05-12 (Avery Johnson): Biggest pain: duplicates and re-notifies. If I mark it ‘Working’, I don’t want another task the next day. Love the ‘Signal summary’ column; please keep it short enough to scan on a laptop.

2025-05-13 (Markus Klein): For ‘Compliance’ and ‘Private/VPC intent’, we should flag as “Needs SE” by default. Add a recommended action line in the note template (e.g., ‘Offer security review + share SOC2 packet’).

2025-05-15 (Sofia Chen): Updated to v0.2: simplified taxonomy to 5 types; moved SE/CS into status to reduce property sprawl; added default filters to exclude existing customers unless expansion-tagged. Shared in Figma and in this ticket description.

2025-05-16 (Tyler Benson): Marketing suppression: if Marketing nurture is active, we should avoid AE outreach unless signal priority is High. Can we add a column/property ‘Active nurture = true’ later? For pilot, ok to handle with suppression rules/workflows.

2025-05-21 (Nikhil Sharma): Marking done. This unblocks Ops to implement the saved views + properties in HubSpot for NA pilot. Engineering will handle suppression semantics in routing service; Sales enablement will incorporate the triage steps into the playbook.
